{
  "summary": "This pull request implements the OP_CAT opcode in Tapscript according to BIP-347 by redefining opcode OP_SUCCESS126 (0x7e). It introduces two script flags, SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT for consensus evaluation and SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT for mempool policy, while omitting miner signaling or activation parameters. The change also adds helper macros to the JSON script test runner to simplify writing Tapscript test cases alongside unit and functional tests.",
  "problem": "Bitcoin Script currently lacks string and byte concatenation operations, which were disabled in 2010 over memory exhaustion concerns. BIP-347 proposes reintroducing OP_CAT in Tapscript with explicit bounds enforced by the 520-byte stack element limit, but Bitcoin Core lacks the interpreter logic and test harness to evaluate or eventually deploy the proposal.",
  "evidence": [
    "Author notes the implementation matches BIP-347 and BIN-2024-0001, which was merged into bitcoin-inquisition on April 25, 2024, activated on Signet on April 30, 2024, and reviewed in the Bitcoin Core PR Review Club.",
    "Author description highlights live Signet testing: 'Since Apr 30 2024 there have been many OP_CAT transactions created and spent on signet.'",
    "Author emphasizes this PR deliberately omits consensus activation: 'This PR does not include miner activation functionality... If this PR is merged it is not a signal of community consensus around activating CAT'."
  ],

It allows concatenation of stack elements up to the 520-byte maximum script element size under a new script verification flag, while keeping OP_CAT discouraged under standard mempool relay policy and disabled on legacy script types. result.summary: This pull request implements the OP_CAT opcode in Tapscript according to BIP-347 by redefining opcode OP_SUCCESS126 (0x7e). It introduces two script flags, SCRIPT_VERIFY_OP_CAT for consensus evaluation and SCRIPT_VERIFY_DISCOURAGE_OP_CAT for mempool policy, while omitting miner signaling or activation parameters. The change also adds helper macros to the JSON script test runner to simplify writing Tapscript test cases alongside unit and functional tests.
result.problem: Bitcoin Script currently lacks string and byte concatenation operations, which were disabled in 2010 over memory exhaustion concerns. BIP-347 proposes reintroducing OP_CAT in Tapscript with explicit bounds enforced by the 520-byte stack element limit, but Bitcoin Core lacks the interpreter logic and test harness to evaluate or eventually deploy the proposal.
evidence: Author notes the implementation matches BIP-347 and BIN-2024-0001, which was merged into bitcoin-inquisition on April 25, 2024, activated on Signet on April 30, 2024, and reviewed in the Bitcoin Core PR Review Club.
Author description highlights live Signet testing: 'Since Apr 30 2024 there have been many OP_CAT transactions created and spent on signet.'

Author emphasizes this PR deliberately omits consensus activation: 'This PR does not include miner activation functionality... If this PR is merged it is not a signal of community consensus around activating CAT'.

enables: Deployment and activation mechanism for BIP-347 OP_CAT

result.scope_notes: Modifies core script execution in interpreter.cpp and policy flags in policy.h. It also extends test/script_tests.cpp with custom string substitution tokens (#SCRIPT#, #CONTROLBLOCK#, #TAPROOTOUTPUT#) to auto-generate Tapscript outputs and control blocks in script_tests.json.
result.card: This pull request implements OP_CAT in Tapscript according to BIP-347 by redefining OP_SUCCESS126. It allows concatenation of stack elements up to the 520-byte maximum script element size under a new script verification flag, while keeping OP_CAT discouraged under standard mempool relay policy and disabled on legacy script types. It does not include consensus activation parameters or miner signaling. The change enables developers and researchers to evaluate and test the opcode implementation directly in Core, following its activation on bitcoin-inquisition Signet in April 2024.
